Add CPRD Aurum code browser tables to CodeMiner database

Source: R/add_cprd_aurum.R
add_cprd_aurum.Rd

Reads a CPRD Aurum code browser release and adds the medcode and prodcode lookup tables, and their mappings to SNOMED CT and Read v2, to the active CodeMiner database. This is a convenience wrapper around read_cprd_aurum() that calls add_lookup_table() and add_mapping_table(). Tables that already exist for the version are skipped.

Usage

add_cprd_aurum(
  path,
  tables = cprd_aurum_tables(),
  version = NULL,
  source = "CPRD Aurum code browser"
)

Arguments

path

Path to the CPRD Aurum code browser release directory, containing CPRDAurumMedical.txt and CPRDAurumProduct.txt. Only the files needed for tables must be present.

tables

Character vector of tables to read. Any of "cprd_aurum_medcode_lkp", "cprd_aurum_prodcode_lkp", "cprd_aurum_medcode_snomed", "cprd_aurum_medcode_read2" and "cprd_aurum_prodcode_snomed". Defaults to all of them. The medcode tables come from CPRDAurumMedical.txt and the prodcode tables from CPRDAurumProduct.txt.

version

Character string for the version label. If NULL (default), the release date (yyyymm) is taken from a directory name like CPRD_CodeBrowser_YYYYMM_Aurum, with a message saying which version is used. If the name doesn't include a release date, an error asks for version to be supplied.

source

Character string for the data source.

Value

Invisibly returns the result from read_cprd_aurum() for the tables that were added (a named list of tables with metadata), or NULL if they all existed already.

Details

CPRD supplies the code browser to researchers with access to its data, so path is required. Check your CPRD data access agreement before sharing a database that contains these tables.

See also

read_cprd_aurum()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
build_database()
add_cprd_aurum("path/to/CPRD_CodeBrowser_YYYYMM_Aurum")
} # }
